purpose: Independent practice of C2.1 (variables in real life).
student_learning_goal: I can describe how variables are used in real-life contexts.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can describe how variables are used in real-life contexts.
header.character_watermark: Eddy in the top-right corner. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Identify the variable in 6 real-life examples. Underline each.
parts.visual_layout: Top of page. Six example rows.

image_placeholders.description: Six rows in B&W line-art, ~7in x 3in. Pre-filled examples: 'T = temperature today (5°C)', 'S = Leafs score (4 goals)', 'A = your age (8 years)', 'P = price of milk ($4.50)', 'D = days till summer (60)', 'W = weight in kg (28)'. Header 'Identify the Variable:'.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P1_FIND: keywords (variable) name what the rows ask for.

parts.answer_key: T, S, A, P, D, W.

parts.student_instructions: Sort 6 variables into UNKNOWN (one fixed value we need to find) or VARYING (changes over time).
parts.visual_layout: Middle of page. Six sort rows.

image_placeholders.description: Six sort rows in B&W line-art, ~7in x 2.5in. Pre-filled: '5 + n = 12', 'Temperature each day', '? - 8 = 6', 'Hockey score per game', 'm + 4 = 9', 'Price of bread weekly'. Each with U/V bubbles. Header 'Unknown (U) or Varying (V)?'.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P2_SORT: keywords (unknown, varying) name the bubbles.

parts.answer_key: U, V, U, V, U, V.

parts.student_instructions: Write 3 variables from your own life. Describe what each one stands for.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of page. Three blank slots.

image_placeholders.description: Three numbered slots in B&W line-art, ~7in x 2.5in. Each: 'Variable: ___', 'Stands for: ___'. Header 'My Variables:'.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P3_OWN: keywords (my, variables) name what the slots ask for.

parts.answer_key: Open. Each variable should stand for a real-life value.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, write a 4-day temperature pattern using the variable T.
teacher_notes: Lesson 1 worksheet. Watch for letter-as-label confusion. Part 2 includes 1-2 transfer contexts (gas-tank g, ice-cream scoops s) not seen in lesson stations — verifies variable naming generalises beyond rehearsed contexts.
